 Metallica only has three more Sphere shows in 2026. Get tickets today 
 By 
 Matt Levy 
 Published 
 Oct. 30, 2026, 5:54 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 Getty Images 
 New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you click or buy through our links. Featured pricing is subject to change.
 There’s just “One” more No Repeat Weekend at Sphere for Metallica in 2026.
 The Rock Hall of Famers’ last three concerts at the visually-stunning venue this year are scheduled to take place:
 Saturday, Oct. 31 
 8:30 p.m. 
 Thursday, Nov. 5 
 8:30 p.m. 
 Saturday, Nov. 7 
 8:30 p.m. 
 If you’d like to see James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo shred live, last-minute tickets are available for all three gigs.
 At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on seats for any of these shows was $341 including fees on Vivid Seats.
 No Repeat Weekend passes — that get you into the Nov. 5 and 7 concerts — start at $902 including fees .
 Should you attend on Thursday, you’ll likely catch a 16-song performance including “Master of Puppets,” “Seek & Destroy,” “Sad But True,” “Ride the Lightning” and “Nothing Else Matters,” based on our findings from past shows at Set List FM .
 Set List FM reports their Saturday shows consist of “Enter Sandman,” “For Whom The Bell Tolls,” “The Unforgiven,” “Fuel” and, of course, “One.”
 And, while the songs are unimpeachable classics, the real draw here is how the music is amplified by Sphere’s larger-than-life wraparound visuals and sound system.
 “Even the most seasoned follower of metal’s biggest group could not be prepared for the visual onslaught of what’s to come across these two, no-repeat nights,” Rock Sound raved after seeing the heavy group in Sin City. 
 “Most memorable is the double-header of ‘For Whom The Bell Tolls’ and ‘One’, accompanied by black and white war imagery as planes fly overhead, clock towers crumble and we roam through the mud trodden trenches. A fully immersive musical experience that is simply astonishing to witness in person.”
 Now this sounds like “One” truly can’t-miss experience.
 For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about Metallica’s 2026-27 Life Burns Faster Las Vegas Sphere residency below.
 Editor’s Note: Metallica returns to Sphere on Jan. 28, 2027. They have shows at the venue scheduled through March 13, 2027 as of now.

 When is Metallica at the Mohegan Sun Arena?
 On top of the residency, Metallica is also helping Uncasville, CT’s cozy 10,000-seat Mohegan Sun Arena celebrate the venue’s 25th anniversary in November.
 This will be the first time the Rock Hall of Famers have performed in the Constitution State since July 1998, when they headlined at Hartford’s Meadows Music Theater as part of their ‘Poor Re-Touring Me Tour.’

 Who else is coming to Sphere?
 When Metallica isn’t lighting up the Sphere stage, many other exciting shows are headed to Vegas’ premier entertainment destination.
 Here’s what’s up next at the one-of-a-kind venue.

 If you’re planning a Las Vegas trip, you can find a complete calendar of all upcoming events at Sphere here .

 Metallica new music
 On April 14, 2023, Metallica dropped their 11th studio album “72 Seasons.”
 The thrumming, high-velocity record quickly sets the tone with the non-stop thrill ride title track and then refuses to let up throughout its healthy 77-minute runtime.
 Indisputable highlights include the snaking “Sleepwalk My Life Away,” nakedly raw “You Must Burn!” and unrelenting “Lux Æterna.” Don’t expect a second to breathe; Metallica goes hard the entire time with nary a moment to rest. Just the way it should be.
 To hear for yourself, you can listen to “72 Seasons” here .
